summary: Independently confirmed all 6 prior reviews' findings are real. Found a new CRITICAL, previously unlisted regression: suspendTenant() re-enters getState()/applyOverrideAndEscalation() before its own UPDATE runs, causing unbounded recursion (RangeError/stack overflow, 500s, and the tenant permanently stuck unable to ever actually be persisted as suspended) for any payment_grace/read_only tenant that crosses the suspend threshold -- triggerable by a single ordinary HTTP request through BillingEnforcementGuard or by DunningService's daily sweep, no concurrency required. Also confirmed getState() is a genuine CQS-violating query-with-side-effect (traced: its write is conditional on real threshold crossings, not an unconditional per-request UPDATE, so that specific framing in the brief is refuted for the non-transition case). Found 2 additional legacy tenants.active readers beyond the ones already catalogued (leads.service.ts public registration lookup, autentique.service.ts webhook) that remain permanently neutered by the same root cause. Found the dunning dedup-key comment is factually inaccurate: updated_at is bumped by idempotent re-entrant writes in suspendTenant/startPaymentGrace, not only on real status transitions, which can produce duplicate notification jobIds outside the already-confirmed staleness scenario. This must not ship.
